metadata.purpose: Canonical project memory for an AI reasoning graph expressed through a 3D editor.
metadata.audience: An AI reasoning over concepts, context, spatial relationships, and open questions.
metadata.core_question: How can spatial relationships preserve the structure of a person's thinking when shared with an AI?
working_principles: Relationships are first-class data, not visual decoration.
Every edit should be saved to the graph document.
The spatial canvas should stay calm and uncluttered.
The graph should be self-describing: concepts, context, positions, and relationship labels should stand on their own without interpreting pixels.
The frontend is a human adaptation of the graph, never a second knowledge layer.

implementation.persistence: Local storage and graph export using thought-network.graph.json as the document shape
implementation.interaction: Orbit canvas, drag bubbles, double-click to create, C to connect, right-click to delete

bubbles.title: Shared brain
bubbles.detail: This is a shared thought network: a person constructs a mental model spatially, then an AI can inspect the same concepts and relationships as structured data.

bubbles.title: AI-readable graph document
bubbles.detail: The save file is a normalized document with stable bubble IDs, semantic context, world positions, colors, types, and labeled connections. It is the project's canonical reasoning surface.

bubbles.title: Spatial thinking
bubbles.detail: 3D position communicates proximity, clusters, distance, and perspective. The canvas is for constructing and revising a mental model rather than decorating a diagram.

bubbles.title: AI reasoning substrate
bubbles.detail: The graph is the canonical reasoning substrate. The interface is only a human-friendly projection for constructing, inspecting, and revising it; it does not contain a separate human layer or AI layer.

bubbles.title: Calm canvas
bubbles.detail: The interface should avoid permanent inspector chrome, creation clutter, and accidental movement. Editing should happen in spatial panels attached to the relevant bubble.

bubbles.title: Relationship semantics
bubbles.detail: A line needs a label such as shapes, informs, challenges, or related to. Future versions should make labels editable so the AI can distinguish causal, evidential, temporal, and associative links.

bubbles.title: Import and versioning
bubbles.detail: The next durable step is file import plus graph history, so a network can travel between sessions, tools, and AI conversations without relying only on browser local storage.

bubbles.title: UI changes
bubbles.detail: The human adaptation should stay quiet and direct: spatial bubbles, minimal chrome, natural editing, and gestures that preserve the feeling of thinking in a field.

bubbles.title: How to use this
bubbles.detail: Use Mindfield as a portable reasoning layer for other work: capture concepts here, connect their meaning, then let a project-specific tool read the graph instead of rebuilding context from scratch.

bubbles.title: Fusion 360 add-in
bubbles.detail: A project adapter could read selected graph concepts as design intent, constraints, or manufacturing decisions, then write observations and open questions back into the same graph.

bubbles.title: VS Code integration
bubbles.detail: Package Mindfield as a reusable workspace companion: open the graph beside code, expose project context to agents, and persist the graph in the repository so setup is not repeated.

bubbles.title: Web or local app
bubbles.detail: Start as a local-first web app with a portable graph file. A future hosted mode can sync graphs, but the canonical document should remain inspectable and usable without a service.
